newsitem.title: GREECE: Short-end of Greek yield curve firms on auction.
newsitem.headline: Short-end of Greek yield curve firms on auction.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were trading higher 10 to 15 basis points in late trade on concerns that an auction of FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds next week will strain liquidity, traders said.
"Shorts are up 10 to 15 basis points on liquidity concerns," said a trader at a foreign bank. "The market is already short and news of an auction next week have amplified the effect."
Greece will auction about 300 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds next week, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters on Monday.
A finance ministry statement said 100 billion drachmas of five-year fixed coupon bonds, the first ever, will be auctioned.
The central bank injected overnight cash at 13.40 percent to smooth out the market.
The mark was quoted at 157.85/95 drachmas from Monday's 158.065 fix, the dollar at 237.26/36 drachmas from 237.770 and the Ecu at 302.45/55 from 302.510 drachmas.
"Banks bought some ecus for drachmas at the fixing and ecu/drachma was allowed to go up further," said a forex trader.
